instructions.question: Does `text` have the rough edges of an unedited human draft: awkward or clunky phrasing, needless repetition, run-on or loose sentences, over-explaining, or small slips?
instructions.focus: Judge how the writing is made, not its topic, its opinions or its punctuation marks.

true.what: At least one sentence a careful editor would smooth out
examples: It shows how much he cares about being a good dad to him.
The quality and the speed was really much better then expected

false.what: Every sentence is smooth, balanced and deliberate

instructions.question: How crafted and polished is the writing in `text`?
instructions.focus: Judge how the writing is made, not its topic, its opinions or its punctuation marks.

criteria: Plain and functional: says things directly, sometimes clumsily or at length
Clear and competent, with little ornament
Polished: balanced sentences and a few crafted lines
Highly crafted: aphorisms, figures of speech and quotable lines throughout

instructions.question: Does `text` end on a crafted closing line: a short, quotable punchline or reveal placed last for effect?
instructions.focus: Judge how the writing is made, not its topic, its opinions or its punctuation marks.

true.what: The last sentence is a polished button, kicker, twist or callback
examples: That was the last time I saw it.

false.what: It just stops, or ends on an ordinary sentence that carries on the narration, argument or post

instructions.question: Does `text` use a crafted figure of speech: a fresh metaphor, simile or personification chosen for effect?
instructions.focus: Judge how the writing is made, not its topic, its opinions or its punctuation marks.

true.what: An inventive image a plain writer would not reach for
examples: her laugh was a door slamming somewhere far away

false.what: Plain literal language, or only everyday idioms and dead metaphors ("fell in love", "a lot on my mind")

instructions.question: Does `text` lean on filler hedges or softeners (I guess, kind of, sort of, pretty much, or whatever, I don't know) more than once?
instructions.focus: Judge how the writing is made, not its topic, its opinions or its punctuation marks.

true.what: Two or more filler hedges or softeners

false.what: None or one, even if the tone is casual

instructions.question: Does `text` repeat the same noun or phrase in close succession where a writer would normally use a pronoun or say it once?
instructions.focus: Judge how the writing is made, not its topic, its opinions or its punctuation marks.

true.what: A noun or phrase repeated mechanically within a sentence or two

false.what: Repetition only for rhetorical effect, or none

instructions.question: Does `text` over-explain: spell out reasons, logistics or feelings the reader could already infer?
instructions.focus: Judge how the writing is made, not its topic, its opinions or its punctuation marks.

true.what: At least one sentence that states the obvious or explains an inference

instructions.question: Does `text` contain a run-on sentence or a comma splice joining two complete clauses?
instructions.focus: Judge how the writing is made, not its topic, its opinions or its punctuation marks.

true.what: Two independent clauses joined by only a comma, or a sentence that runs on loosely

instructions.question: Does `text` set a short dramatic line or inner thought as its own paragraph for emphasis?
instructions.focus: Judge how the writing is made, not its topic, its opinions or its punctuation marks.

true.what: A one-line paragraph used for a beat, reveal or thought
